scenicChapters.title: Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2094 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: 2474 m come off over 27 km at around 7.4%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: For 44 km this is Stelvio Pass, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 122.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2757 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Passo di Croce Domini
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 70 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

scenicChapters.title: The Via Appia on the route from Beneventum → 18th-Century Royal Palace
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 69 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
